title: Modern Linux mechanisms
baseline: Linux 0.11 historical comparison plus current Linux kernel documentation. Modern implementation details are not presented as 0.11 APIs.

claims.claim: Modern physical memory is organized by nodes and zones; the buddy allocator manages free page blocks by order.

source.symbol: nodes, zones, free_area and buddy allocator

claims.claim: SLUB/slab object cache debugging supports red zoning, poisoning, user tracking and slabinfo; enabling debugging has overhead.
CFS was merged in Linux 2.6.23 and tracks weighted virtual runtime using a time-ordered red-black tree.
Linux began transitioning to EEVDF in 6.6; selection first considers eligibility/lag, then earliest virtual deadline.
module_init/module_exit distinguish built-in initcalls and module insertion/removal; modules execute in kernel context.
External modules should be built through Kbuild against the configured target kernel build tree.
The eBPF verifier tracks register and pointer states and checks memory bounds/alignment and helper arguments.

source.symbol: verifier state tracking and pointer bounds

claims.claim: BPF maps provide typed shared storage accessible to BPF programs and user space.
AF_XDP uses UMEM and FILL/COMPLETION/RX/TX rings; XDP_ZEROCOPY requests zero-copy and fails if unavailable.
XDP metadata and PASS/redirect paths have driver-specific semantics; the XDP path is not a replacement for the whole TCP/IP stack.
